reason: Published 2026-10-30; fixed only in glob 14.0.2, a major version. The copy (13.0.6) comes from expo-updates, @expo/cli, @expo/config, @expo/config-plugins, @expo/fingerprint and @expo/metro-config, which run on a developer or build machine (expo start, export, prebuild, fingerprinting). glob reads the file system, so it is not in the phone app or the web bundle. The flaw needs a caller that cancels a glob with an AbortSignal; these tools do not. npm's only offered fix is an old expo-updates. Re-check when Expo moves to glob 14 (expected with SDK 58), then drop this exception.

Published 2026-10-30; fixed only in minimatch 11.0.1, a major version. The copy (10.2.6) is glob 13's, under the same Expo build tools as GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 above, and runs only on a developer or build machine with our own project's patterns, never with input from users. The flaw is a slow match on crafted patterns (denial of service), with no data exposure. Re-check together with the glob exception above.

Patched in uuid 11.1.1, but the old copies come from @expo/ngrok (uuid 3, used only for `expo start --tunnel`) and xcode (uuid 7, used by iOS config plugins during a build). They need the old uuid API, so forcing 11 could break those build tools and there is no Android or iOS build on this machine to prove it does not. The flaw only matters when a caller passes a buffer to v3, v5 or v6, which these tools do not. Re-check when Expo updates those packages.

Fixed in decode-uri-component 0.5.0, but we cannot use it yet. The copy (0.2.2) is a transitive dependency of expo-router, which uses query-string 7 to read query strings when it matches links and route paths in the phone apps (not the web build, which never loads expo-router). No code of ours calls query-string or decode-uri-component, and we have not shown a link that triggers the slow decode; the flaw is a denial of service (slow decoding of malformed percent-encoded text), with no data exposure. 0.5.0 is ES-module only and query-string 7 loads it with require(), and query-string 9 has no named exports, which expo-router calls (tried and backed out; it would break link and route parsing). Re-check when expo-router moves off query-string 7 or a compatible fix ships, and then drop this exception.

Published 2026-10-30; no patched release exists (every version up to 0.5.0, the latest, is affected). npm's only suggested fix is expo-router 58, a major Expo SDK upgrade. It is the same copy as GHSA-vcc3-ghjq-m6fr above (0.2.2, via expo-router > query-string 7), used only to read query strings when expo-router matches links and route paths in the phone apps; the web build never loads expo-router and no code of ours calls it. The flaw is a denial of service (slow decoding of long percent-encoded runs), with no data exposure. Re-check when a fixed decode-uri-component ships or when moving to Expo SDK 58, and then drop this exception.

Our own copy is fixed: @taskdrop/schemas uses zod 4.6.7. The copy that is left (zod 3.25.76) is a dependency of @expo/cli, which asks for zod ^3.25.76; the advisory's only patched release is 4.6.6, and forcing zod 4 on Expo's CLI could break its dev server, which cannot be proved here without a full build. The CLI uses it only for its DevTools plugin and MCP extension schemas (DevToolsPlugin.schema.js, createMCPDevToolsExtensionSchema.js) on a developer or build machine; it is not part of the shipped app, the web bundle or any Edge Function. The flaw is a memory-exhaustion denial of service when validating oversized constrained collections. Re-check when @expo/cli moves to zod 4.
